title: Max's Ski Week and Spring Break
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for the McKinley Bulldogs.

pages: McKinley has two breaks that Max looks forward to all year. In February there is Ski Week, a whole week off in the middle of winter. In spring there is Spring Break. This year, Max's family has plans for both, and Max has promised the class a full report when school starts again.

For Ski Week, the family drives up to the mountains near Lake Tahoe. Max has never skied before. In ski school, the instructor teaches the beginners two shapes. "Pizza" means pointing your ski tips together in a wedge to slow down. "French fries" means keeping your skis straight to go faster. Max's first run is mostly pizza, a little bit of french fries, and one very big face-plant into the snow.

By the third day, Max can ride the chairlift and make it down the green run without falling. At the bottom, Max celebrates with hot chocolate and a giant pretzel. That night, Max writes in a journal: "Skiing is like reading. At first every word is hard, and then one day you just glide."

Spring Break is quieter. Max visits the library and checks out a stack of books, plants new seeds in the garden boxes at home, and goes to the beach with Lupe's family. One rainy afternoon, Max builds a cardboard model of McKinley, complete with the MPR, the field, and a tiny paper Max waving from the front office.

When school starts again, Max gives the report. Max shows photos of the snow, reads the journal entry out loud, and passes around the cardboard school. The teacher says, "It sounds like you rested, explored, and learned something new." Max nods. "Breaks are great," Max says. "But honestly, I missed McKinley."
